news.title: New Zealand to help more schools recruit international students
news.summary_en: New Zealand is investing up to NZ$2.5 million in a new support service designed to help more schools recruit, enrol and retain international students from 2027, as the government pushes ahead with ambitious international education growth targets.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: The PIE Live Germany marks Deutschland’s rise as a ‘top four’ study destination
news.summary_en: As Germany breaks into the ‘big four’ – surpassing Canada in new international enrolments – The PIE lands in Berlin to explore what lies ahead. The PIE Live Germany will take place on 30 October 2026 at GLS Hotel Oderberger. Here’s what to expect from the lineup in what promises to be a stellar event!
news.author: Nicholas Cuthbert

news.title: US: OPT fee proposal exposes divide in Indian applicants
news.summary_en: Proposed OPT fees threaten the appeal of US study for Indian students relying on loans, but advisers report mixed responses among applicants.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: Unis must adapt partnerships as China reshapes market
news.summary_en: Universities risk losing appeal to Chinese students unless they adapt their teaching and expand transnational education partnerships, a recruitment expert has warned.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: Germany’s growing appeal spans diverse routes into study and work
news.summary_en: Germany’s appeal as an international education destination is being strengthened by its diverse university offering and pathways into employment – but the experience of studying and recruiting there varies considerably between public and private institutions, and according to students’ country of origin.
news.author: Amy Baker

news.title: 70% of visa refusals for UK study visas come from seven countries
news.summary_en: More than 70% of study visa refusals for UK universities are coming from just seven countries – India, Nigeria, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Ghana and Sri Lanka. The PIE looks at which universities are the most reliant on high-risk markets.
news.author: Nicholas Cuthbert and Dave Amor

news.title: Dia duit from Dublin! All the news from The PIE Live Ireland
news.summary_en: The PIE's editor Beth Kennedy breaks down the key takeaways from The PIE's second PIE Live Ireland conference.
news.author: The PIE News team

news.title: When UK compliance changes, who carries the cost of late communication?
news.summary_en: Compliance may be a headache for UK institutions, argues Tuba Naeem. But there's always a student on the other end who pays the real price.
news.author: Tuba Naeem

news.title: Protecting the metric, damaging the mission
news.summary_en: Compliance experts Alex Lock and Mike Strong argue that unintended consequences linked to fulfilling BCA metrics are damaging the UK's overall mission for sustainable recruitment and quality, as set out in the International Education Strategy.
news.author: Alex Lock and Mike Strong

news.title: Telangana courts international campuses for ‘Future City’
news.summary_en: Telangana has ordered officials to draw up a policy to attract international universities to its proposed Future City development, although the University of Birmingham and University of London, both named in media reports citing state officials, have yet to confirm campus commitments.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: Unis urged to build deeper international partnerships amid geopolitical uncertainty
news.summary_en: Universities must invest in long-term, mutually beneficial international partnerships to maintain public trust and deliver meaningful research and economic outcomes amid geopolitical uncertainty, higher education leaders have said.
news.author: The PIE News team
